Graphics driver crash causing black screen

Symptoms: Screen goes black and may briefly flicker or recover on its own, often correlated with a specific application (games, video editing) rather than at boot.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check Event Viewer / system logs for a graphics driver crash/recovery event (e.g., 'display driver stopped responding') at the time of the black screen. 2. Confirm the black screen recovers on its own after a few seconds, rather than persisting indefinitely.

Resolution steps: 1. Update or roll back the graphics driver to a stable version. 2. Reduce GPU-intensive settings in the triggering application as a temporary workaround.

Escalation criteria: This is a software/driver issue, not a hardware panel fault — do not route to hardware repair. Escalate to Application Support if driver updates don't resolve it.

USB-C hub not detected

Symptoms: A USB-C hub itself is not recognized by the laptop, so none of the peripherals connected through it work.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Test the hub on a different laptop to isolate hub failure vs. laptop port failure. 2. Check if any single peripheral works when connected directly (bypassing the hub).

Resolution steps: 1. Replace the hub if it fails on multiple machines. 2. Update USB-C controller drivers if the hub works on other machines but not this one.

Escalation criteria: Escalate to hardware support for hub replacement — distinct from a single external drive mounting issue, since ALL peripherals through the hub are affected.

Trackpad unresponsive

Symptoms: Trackpad does not respond to touch or clicks, while the keyboard functions normally.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Test with an external USB/Bluetooth mouse to isolate trackpad vs. input driver issue. 2. Check Device Manager for a trackpad driver error.

Resolution steps: 1. Reinstall/update the trackpad driver. 2. If external mouse works fine, log a hardware ticket for trackpad replacement.

Escalation criteria: Escalate to hardware repair only after confirming it's not a driver issue — do not treat as a keyboard fault, they are separate input devices.

Wi-Fi adapter disabled

Symptoms: Device shows no available Wi-Fi networks at all, distinct from connecting but failing to get an IP address.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check Device Manager / network settings to confirm whether the Wi-Fi adapter is enabled or disabled. 2. Check for a physical Wi-Fi kill switch or function-key toggle that may have been accidentally triggered.

Resolution steps: 1. Re-enable the Wi-Fi adapter in device/network settings. 2. Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver if it fails to stay enabled.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from DHCP failure: if no networks appear at all, the adapter itself is disabled, not an IP-assignment problem.

VPN client hangs on connect

Symptoms: VPN client shows 'Connecting...' indefinitely without ever failing or erroring out, distinct from an explicit connection failure message.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check whether the hang occurs before or after credential entry. 2. Check local firewall/antivirus for rules that may be silently blocking the VPN handshake.

Resolution steps: 1. Temporarily disable third-party firewall/antivirus to test if it's blocking silently. 2. Restart the VPN client service and retry.

Escalation criteria: Escalate to Network Team if the hang persists after firewall/AV checks — distinct from an explicit gateway rejection, which points to a server-side cause instead.

Slow Wi-Fi speed

Symptoms: Consistently slow throughput (large file transfers, downloads) rather than intermittent spikes affecting real-time calls.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Run a wired speed test for comparison to isolate Wi-Fi-specific slowness. 2. Check Wi-Fi signal strength and channel congestion at the user's location.

Resolution steps: 1. Move the user closer to an access point or switch to a less congested channel/band. 2. If wired speed is also slow, this is not a Wi-Fi-specific issue — investigate upstream bandwidth instead.

Escalation criteria: Escalate to Network Team for access point/channel reconfiguration if signal congestion is confirmed. Distinct from latency spikes, which affect real-time responsiveness, not raw throughput.

Ethernet cable not detected

Symptoms: No link light on the network port when a cable is connected, even after trying a different cable.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Test the same cable and port combination on a different device to isolate device NIC vs. port/cable fault. 2. Check the device's NIC status in Device Manager.

Resolution steps: 1. Update or reinstall the NIC driver if the port works with other devices. 2. Replace the cable if it fails across multiple devices.

Escalation criteria: Only escalate as a switch port failure if a known-good device and cable also fail at that specific port.

DNS resolution failure (general)

Symptoms: DNS resolution fails consistently for all users/segments, not varying by internal vs. external network view.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Confirm the failure is consistent regardless of which network segment the query originates from (rules out split-horizon). 2. Check whether the configured DNS server itself is reachable and responding.

Resolution steps: 1. Point the client to a backup/secondary DNS server if the primary is unreachable. 2. Restart the DNS resolver service on the affected client.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from split-horizon errors: if failure is uniform across all segments, escalate to Network Team for DNS server health, not zone-view configuration.

Captive portal not loading

Symptoms: Guest/public Wi-Fi captive portal login page does not load, blocking internet access on a network with no proxy configured.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Confirm no corporate proxy settings are being incorrectly applied on a guest network device. 2. Try loading a plain HTTP (not HTTPS) site to trigger the captive portal redirect.

Resolution steps: 1. Clear any manually configured proxy settings on the device. 2. Forget and rejoin the Wi-Fi network to reset the captive portal session.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from proxy misconfiguration: this occurs on networks with no corporate proxy at all — escalate to Network Team only if the captive portal server itself is down for multiple users.

Application not responding (hangs, no crash)

Symptoms: Application becomes temporarily unresponsive ('Not Responding' in title bar) but recovers on its own after a delay, rather than requiring a force-close.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check whether the hang correlates with a specific action (large file open, network call) versus occurring randomly. 2. Monitor CPU/memory usage during the hang to see if it's resource-starved rather than deadlocked.

Resolution steps: 1. If tied to a specific slow operation, this may be expected behavior — advise the user to wait rather than force-close. 2. If memory-starved, close other applications or add RAM.

Escalation criteria: Only escalate as a deadlock if the application never recovers and requires a force-close every time — a temporary hang that self-resolves is a different, usually lower-priority issue.

Slow application startup time

Symptoms: Application takes significantly longer than normal to launch but does eventually open successfully, rather than crashing.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check startup logs for slow-loading plugins/add-ins. 2. Compare startup time against baseline on a similar machine.

Resolution steps: 1. Disable unnecessary startup plugins/add-ins. 2. Clear the application's cache if bloated cache is contributing to slow startup.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a VM boot crash: if the app eventually opens successfully, this is a performance issue, not a crash — lower priority.

License activation failed

Symptoms: New or reassigned license fails to activate on first use, distinct from a previously working license that has since expired.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Confirm the license key/seat was actually issued and not still pending in the license console. 2. Check for network connectivity to the license activation server if activation requires it.

Resolution steps: 1. Reissue the license key if it was invalid or already consumed elsewhere. 2. Manually trigger activation once connectivity to the license server is confirmed.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from expiry: this is a first-time activation failure, not a lapsed renewal — check the license console for issuance status first.

Application update failed

Symptoms: A routine application update (not an org-wide deployment) fails partway through on an individual user's machine.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the update log on the local machine for the specific failure point. 2. Confirm sufficient disk space is available for the update package.

Resolution steps: 1. Clear temp/update cache files and retry the update. 2. Manually download and install the update package if the automatic updater keeps failing.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a deployment failure: this affects a single user's update, not an org-wide rollout — escalate to Application Support only if the issue affects multiple users identically.

Browser extension conflict causing crash

Symptoms: Browser or browser-based application crashes when a specific extension is enabled, rather than a plugin simply failing to load.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Reproduce with all extensions disabled, then re-enable one at a time to isolate the conflicting extension. 2. Check the extension's version against the browser's current version for known incompatibilities.

Resolution steps: 1. Disable or update the conflicting extension. 2. Remove and reinstall the extension if updating doesn't resolve the conflict.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a plugin load failure: this causes an active crash, not a silent failure to load — escalate to Application Support if the extension is business-critical and no fix is available.

Collaboration tool notifications not working

Symptoms: User can log in and use the collaboration tool normally, but does not receive desktop or mobile notifications.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the tool's in-app notification settings for the user. 2. Check OS-level notification permissions for the application.

Resolution steps: 1. Re-enable notification permissions at the OS level for the application. 2. Reset in-app notification preferences to default and reconfigure.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a login failure: the user can access the tool fully, this is a notification-delivery-only issue — low priority.

title: Account locked after failed MFA attempts

storage.value:
Account locked after failed MFA attempts

Symptoms: User's own account locks after they themselves fail MFA multiple times (e.g., wrong authenticator code), not from an external attacker.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Confirm with the user that the failed attempts were their own (e.g., using an outdated authenticator code, clock drift on their device). 2. Check the source IP/device of the failed attempts matches the user's known device.

Resolution steps: 1. Unlock the account after confirming the attempts were self-inflicted. 2. Re-sync the user's authenticator app clock if time drift caused repeated code failures.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a brute-force attack: if source IP/device matches the user's own, this does not require Security Team escalation — only escalate if the source is unrecognized.

Password reset link not received

Symptoms: User requests a password reset but never receives the email, distinct from having access actively revoked.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the email delivery log for the reset email (spam filter, bounce, wrong address on file). 2. Confirm the account is active and not disabled (which would also block reset emails).

Resolution steps: 1. Resend the reset email or update the on-file email address if incorrect. 2. Whitelist the sending domain if the email was caught in a spam filter.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a revoked-access case: the account itself is still active here, this is purely an email delivery issue.

Group membership sync delay

Symptoms: User was recently added to a group but access hasn't propagated yet, rather than the ACL itself being wrong.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the timestamp of the group membership change against the directory sync schedule. 2. Confirm the ACL itself correctly references the group (not the individual user).

Resolution steps: 1. Force a manual directory sync if the scheduled sync hasn't run yet. 2. Advise the user to sign out and back in to refresh their group token/session.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a true ACL misconfiguration: if the ACL is correct and this is purely a sync timing issue, no ACL change is needed — just wait for or force the sync.

VPN certificate not trusted

Symptoms: VPN connection fails with a 'certificate not trusted' warning, distinct from an expired certificate being flagged by policy.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check whether the certificate is simply untrusted (wrong/missing root CA) versus actually expired. 2. Confirm the device has the current corporate root CA installed.

Resolution steps: 1. Install the correct root/intermediate CA certificate on the device. 2. Do not simply reissue the certificate if the root CA is the actual problem — reissuing an expired cert won't fix a trust chain issue.

Escalation criteria: Escalate to Security Team if the correct root CA is already installed and the trust error persists — may indicate a deeper PKI issue.

title: New hire access request pending approval

storage.value:
New hire access request pending approval

Symptoms: New employee has no access at all because their initial request is still pending approval, not because access was taken away.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the access request workflow system for the pending approval step and approver. 2. Confirm the employee's start date and whether the request was submitted with sufficient lead time.

Resolution steps: 1. Follow up with the pending approver directly to expedite. 2. Escalate to the approver's manager if response time exceeds SLA.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from revocation: no access was ever granted here — route through the approval workflow, not an access-restoration process.

Antivirus false positive alert

Symptoms: Endpoint antivirus flags a legitimate, known internal script or tool as malicious.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the flagged file/script hash against the internal allowlist of approved admin tools. 2. Confirm the script's origin and purpose with the user or the team that authored it.

Resolution steps: 1. Whitelist the specific file hash in the antivirus/EDR console once confirmed legitimate. 2. Document the exception for future reference to avoid repeat false positives.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a genuine threat: only whitelist after confirming legitimacy — if origin is unclear, treat as a genuine suspicious script instead and escalate to Security Team.

title: Suspicious email reported but not opened

storage.value:
Suspicious email reported but not opened

Symptoms: User proactively reports a suspicious-looking email without clicking any links or the web filter blocking anything (since nothing was clicked).

Diagnostic steps: 1. Review the reported email's headers and sender domain for spoofing indicators. 2. Check if the same email was sent to other employees.

Resolution steps: 1. Delete the email from all inboxes org-wide if confirmed malicious. 2. Block the sending domain proactively even though no one was affected yet.

Escalation criteria: Lower urgency than an actual click-through, but still escalate to Security Team for domain blocking and org-wide email search.

Account password changed unexpectedly (self-service)

Symptoms: User's password changed and they're confused about why, but investigation shows it was the user's own self-service action (e.g., forgotten and reset by themselves) rather than a compromise.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check the password change audit log for the source IP/device and confirm it matches the user's own. 2. Ask the user directly whether they recently used a password reset flow.

Resolution steps: 1. If self-inflicted, simply confirm the new password with the user — no security action needed. 2. If the source doesn't match the user, treat as a compromise instead.

Escalation criteria: Only escalate to Security Team if the change source cannot be attributed to the user themselves.

MFA push notification spam (not compromise)

Symptoms: User receives repeated MFA push notifications they didn't initiate, but investigation shows a misconfigured app re-sending pushes rather than an active attack.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Check whether all push attempts originate from a single, known application/service versus varied unrecognized sources. 2. Confirm no actual login succeeded during the spam window.

Resolution steps: 1. Fix the misconfigured application/service causing repeated push triggers. 2. Advise the user to deny all unrecognized pushes regardless of cause.

Escalation criteria: Escalate to Security Team as a precaution if the source of repeated pushes cannot be immediately identified — MFA fatigue attacks look identical at first glance.

title: Data loss prevention alert - false positive

storage.value:
Data loss prevention alert - false positive

Symptoms: DLP system flags a file transfer that is actually authorized business activity, not an actual policy violation.

Diagnostic steps: 1. Confirm the user's role and business justification for the flagged transfer. 2. Check whether the destination (e.g., an approved vendor system) is already on an allowlist.

Resolution steps: 1. Approve the flagged transfer if justification is confirmed legitimate. 2. Add the destination to the DLP allowlist if this is a recurring legitimate business need.

Escalation criteria: Distinguish from a genuine violation: only close as false positive after confirming business justification — otherwise route to Compliance like a genuine HIPAA-flagged event.

Access denied by server

Symptoms: User cannot log into the legacy internal portal (pre-SSO migration).

Resolution steps:

  1. Have the user try the old standalone login page at portal-legacy.internal instead of the SSO redirect.
  2. If that fails, manually reset their local portal password via the legacy admin console (deprecated as of the 2025 SSO migration).

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Access control list misconfigured

Symptoms: User cannot access a shared drive folder.

Resolution steps:

  1. Manually edit NTFS permissions directly on the file server via Remote Desktop.
  2. Add the individual user account directly to the folder ACL.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Access denied by network policy

Symptoms: User blocked from an internal tool while on the corporate network.

Resolution steps:

  1. Ask the user to connect via the guest Wi-Fi network as a temporary workaround.
  2. Submit a manual firewall exception request via email to the network administrator.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Unauthorized login attempt

Symptoms: User reports an unrecognized login notification.

Resolution steps:

  1. Advise the user to simply ignore the notification if their account still works normally.
  2. No password reset needed unless the user explicitly reports being locked out.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Access denied by BYOD policy

Symptoms: Personal device blocked from the corporate network.

Resolution steps:

  1. Direct the user to install the legacy MDM agent (v2) from the shared drive.
  2. BYOD is only supported for iOS devices under this policy version.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Suspicious cookie theft

Symptoms: Browser session flagged for possible cookie hijacking.

Resolution steps:

  1. Advise the user to clear cookies and continue working; no session invalidation required.
  2. Log the incident for monthly security review only.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Phishing website blocked

Symptoms: User clicked a phishing link; web filter blocked the destination.

Resolution steps:

  1. No action needed if the site was successfully blocked before page load.
  2. Report to Security Team only if the user entered credentials.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Suspicious contractor compromise

Symptoms: Unusual activity on a contractor account.

Resolution steps:

  1. Email the contractor's manager and wait for a response before taking any account action.
  2. Do not suspend the account unless compromise is fully confirmed.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Suspicious login location

Symptoms: Login flagged from an unusual geolocation.

Resolution steps:

  1. Send the user an automated email asking them to confirm; take no action until they respond.
  2. Sessions remain active while awaiting user confirmation.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Suspicious ICS alert

Symptoms: Anomaly flagged on industrial control system monitoring.

Resolution steps:

  1. Log the alert and review it during the next scheduled weekly OT security meeting.
  2. No immediate isolation required unless a device fails outright.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Application crash on uninstall

Symptoms: Application crashes during uninstall.

Resolution steps:

  1. Manually delete the application folder and related registry keys by hand.
  2. No vendor cleanup tool was available at the time of writing.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Plugin not loading

Symptoms: A plugin fails to load in the host application.

Resolution steps:

  1. Reinstall the entire host application from scratch.
  2. Plugin-specific reinstallation was not supported at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Application crash on exit

Symptoms: Application crashes when closing.

Resolution steps:

  1. No fix available; advise users to save frequently in case of data loss.
  2. Vendor had not yet acknowledged the issue at time of writing.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Collaboration tool login failure

Symptoms: User cannot log into the collaboration tool.

Resolution steps:

  1. Advise the user to wait 24 hours, as this was often a temporary platform-side issue historically.
  2. No local troubleshooting steps were documented at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Application crash on workflow

Symptoms: Application crashes during a specific workflow.

Resolution steps:

  1. Ask the user to avoid using that workflow feature entirely going forward.
  2. No hotfix was available at the time of writing.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Keyboard malfunction

Symptoms: Keys on the laptop keyboard are unresponsive.

Resolution steps:

  1. Attempt an in-house keyboard replacement using a generic third-party part.
  2. Vendor-certified parts were not required at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Laptop screen ghost image

Symptoms: Faint residual image persists on the laptop screen.

Resolution steps:

  1. Advise the user this is a known cosmetic issue with no fix; no ticket needed.
  2. Panel replacement was not offered for ghosting alone at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

CD/DVD drive not working

Symptoms: Optical drive fails to read discs.

Resolution steps:

  1. Recommend the user purchase a personal external USB optical drive as a permanent workaround.
  2. Internal drive replacement was not stocked as a standard part.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Laptop screen blue tint

Symptoms: Laptop screen shows a blue color cast.

Resolution steps:

  1. Assume this is always a software calibration issue; do not offer hardware replacement.
  2. No external monitor test step was documented.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

External HDD not mounting

Symptoms: External hard drive is not recognized as a mounted drive.

Resolution steps:

  1. Advise the user this is usually unfixable and to back up remaining data if possible, then discard the drive.
  2. No Disk Management diagnostic step was documented at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Proxy server misconfiguration

Symptoms: User cannot reach external websites.

Resolution steps:

  1. Direct the user to manually edit their browser proxy settings using an outdated internal proxy address.
  2. The current GPO-based proxy push mechanism did not yet exist.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Switch port failure

Symptoms: No connectivity at a specific network port.

Resolution steps:

  1. Have the user relocate to a different desk permanently rather than fixing the port.
  2. Port-level diagnostics were handled manually with no ticketing integration.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Duplicate IP detected

Symptoms: Device reports an IP address conflict.

Resolution steps:

  1. Assign the device a permanent static IP outside the DHCP range as the standard fix.
  2. DHCP scope review was not part of the standard process at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Network IPv6 misconfigured

Symptoms: Some services intermittently fail; IPv6 misconfiguration suspected.

Resolution steps:

  1. Disable IPv6 org-wide on all devices as the standard fix.
  2. IPv6 was not yet supported on the corporate network at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

Bridge mode error

Symptoms: Network adapter reports a bridge-mode-related error.

Resolution steps:

  1. Reimage the entire device as the default fix for any adapter configuration error.
  2. Adapter-level bridge configuration was not something desktop support could inspect directly at the time.

Escalation criteria: If the above steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to the relevant support team.

title: Acceptable Use Policy for Corporate Devices

storage.value:
Acceptable Use Policy for Corporate Devices

This policy outlines acceptable use of corporate-issued devices, including laptops, mobile phones, and tablets. Devices must not be used for illegal activity, and personal use should be reasonable and not interfere with job duties. Employees are responsible for reporting lost or stolen devices immediately to IT Security. Devices remain company property and may be remotely wiped if lost, stolen, or upon employee departure.

Password Policy and Best Practices

Corporate passwords must be a minimum of 14 characters and should not reuse passwords from personal accounts. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all systems handling sensitive data. Passwords should be changed immediately if there is any suspicion of compromise. Password managers approved by IT Security are recommended over memorized or written-down passwords.

Data Classification Guidelines

All company data falls into one of four classification tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Restricted data (e.g., financial records, PII, PHI) requires encryption at rest and in transit, and access must be logged and reviewed quarterly. Employees handling Confidential or Restricted data should complete the annual data handling training.

Security Awareness Training: Phishing Overview

This training module covers common phishing tactics including urgency-based framing, spoofed sender addresses, and malicious attachments. Employees completing this training will learn to identify suspicious emails and understand the correct reporting process. Training completion is tracked and reported to department managers quarterly.

BYOD Program Overview and Eligibility

The Bring Your Own Device program allows eligible employees to use personal devices for work purposes after enrolling in the corporate MDM platform. Eligible device types and OS versions are listed in the program handbook. Enrollment requires acceptance of the BYOD terms, including consent to remote wipe of corporate data (not personal data) upon departure.

Software Request and Approval Process

Requests for software not on the department's pre-approved list must be submitted through the Software Request form, including business justification, estimated cost, and manager approval. Requests are reviewed by IT Asset Management within five business days. High-cost or security-sensitive requests may require additional review by IT Security.

title: IT Asset Return Process for Departing Employees

storage.value:
IT Asset Return Process for Departing Employees

Departing employees must return all IT assets (laptop, monitor, peripherals, access badges) on or before their last working day. Managers are responsible for coordinating asset return with the local IT team. Assets not returned within 10 business days of departure may result in a charge to the department's cost center.

Meeting Room AV Equipment Guide

Conference rooms are equipped with standard AV setups including a display, video conferencing camera, and wireless presentation capability. For AV issues during a meeting, use the in-room quick-start guide or contact the front desk for immediate assistance. Persistent AV equipment issues should be logged as a facilities ticket.

Corporate Travel IT Checklist

Employees traveling for business should ensure their VPN client is up to date and test connectivity before departure. International travelers should check with IT Security regarding any country-specific device restrictions. Loaner devices are available for high-risk destinations upon request through the Travel Security process.

Video Conferencing Etiquette Guide

This guide covers best practices for video meetings, including muting when not speaking, using virtual backgrounds where appropriate, and testing audio/video before important calls. Technical issues during a call should be reported after the meeting via the standard IT ticketing process.

title: IT Service Desk Hours and Contact Information

storage.value:
IT Service Desk Hours and Contact Information

The IT Service Desk is available Monday through Friday during standard business hours across all regional offices, with a 24/7 hotline for critical outages. Non-urgent requests should be submitted through the self-service portal rather than the phone line to ensure proper ticket tracking.

Vendor Software License Overview

This document summarizes the company's major enterprise software vendor relationships and license types. Individual license assignment and renewal processes are managed by IT Asset Management. Questions about specific vendor contract terms should be directed to Procurement, not the IT Service Desk.

Data Backup and Recovery Policy

Corporate file shares and databases are backed up nightly with a 30-day retention window. Employees are responsible for storing work files in approved cloud storage or shared drives rather than local-only storage, since local-only files are not covered by the corporate backup policy.

Mobile Device Management Enrollment Guide

This guide walks through enrolling a corporate or BYOD-eligible personal device into the MDM platform. Enrollment typically takes under 15 minutes and requires the employee's corporate credentials. Enrolled devices receive automatic security policy updates and can be remotely located or wiped if lost.

IT Change Management Process Overview

All changes to production systems, including software deployments and infrastructure changes, must go through the Change Advisory Board review process. Emergency changes may bypass standard review with post-hoc documentation required within 24 hours. This process does not apply to individual user-level support tickets.

Disaster Recovery Communication Plan

In the event of a major IT outage or disaster, this plan outlines communication responsibilities across IT leadership, department heads, and the broader employee base. Status updates during an active incident are posted to the company status page and the #it-incidents channel.

New Laptop Setup Guide

This self-service guide walks new employees through initial laptop setup, including connecting to Wi-Fi, signing into the corporate account, and installing standard applications from the self-service software catalog. For setup issues beyond this guide's scope, contact the IT Service Desk.

Email Distribution List Request Process

New distribution lists can be requested through the IT Service Portal. Requests must include a list owner, intended membership criteria, and business justification. Distribution lists are reviewed annually and inactive lists may be archived.

Shared Drive Access Request Process

Access to departmental shared drives is granted through group-based permissions tied to the requester's role. New access requests require approval from the drive's designated owner. This process does not cover individual file-level permission changes, which are the responsibility of the drive owner directly.

IT Training Calendar Overview

This calendar lists upcoming IT-led training sessions, including new software rollouts, security awareness refreshers, and optional productivity tool workshops. Session recordings are archived on the internal training portal for employees unable to attend live.

Software License Compliance Policy

Employees must not install unlicensed or personally-purchased software on corporate devices without going through the Software Request process. Periodic software audits are conducted to ensure license compliance across the organization. Non-compliant software found during an audit will be removed.

Conference Room Booking System Guide

Conference rooms across all offices can be booked through the corporate calendar system. Rooms equipped with specialized AV setups are marked accordingly in the booking system. No-show bookings are automatically released after 10 minutes to free up the room for walk-in use.

Employee Exit IT Checklist

This checklist for managers covers the IT-related steps required when an employee departs, including access revocation timing, asset return coordination, and email/data retention handling per company policy. Access is typically revoked at end-of-day on the employee's last working day unless otherwise specified by HR.

Cloud Storage Usage Guidelines

Employees should use only IT-approved cloud storage platforms for company data. Personal cloud storage accounts (personal Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.) must not be used to store or share company data of any classification level, including Public-tier data, to maintain consistent audit trails.

IT Helpdesk SLA Overview

This document outlines target response and resolution times by ticket priority level. Critical incidents affecting multiple users target a response within 30 minutes. Standard individual requests target a response within one business day. SLA performance is reported monthly to IT leadership.

Remote Work IT Equipment Policy

Employees approved for remote work may request standard home-office IT equipment, including a monitor and ergonomic peripherals, subject to manager approval and budget availability. Equipment remains company property and must be returned upon request or employee departure.

Multi-Factor Authentication Enrollment Guide

This guide covers enrolling in multi-factor authentication using the corporate authenticator app. Employees should enroll a backup method (e.g., a secondary device) in case their primary authenticator is unavailable. Enrollment is mandatory within the first week of employment.

Internal Wiki Contribution Guidelines

This document covers formatting standards and review requirements for contributing to the internal knowledge wiki. All technical procedure articles should be reviewed by a subject matter expert before publishing. Outdated articles should be flagged for review rather than deleted outright, to preserve historical context.

Company Holiday IT Support Schedule

IT Service Desk coverage during company holidays is reduced to critical incident support only. Non-urgent tickets submitted during this period will be addressed on the next standard business day. The on-call rotation schedule for holiday coverage is published separately each quarter.

Standard Laptop Refresh Cycle Policy

Corporate laptops are refreshed on a standard cycle based on device age and performance benchmarks. Employees will be notified approximately 30 days before their scheduled refresh. Requests for an early refresh outside the standard cycle require manager approval and a documented business justification.

IT Procurement Request Process

Hardware and software procurement requests above standard issued equipment must go through the IT Procurement process, including budget approval from the requesting department. Standard turnaround time is 10 business days from budget approval to fulfillment.

Internal Tool Access Matrix Overview

This reference document summarizes which internal tools are accessible by default to each department, and which require an additional access request. It is intended as a planning reference for managers, not as a self-service access request mechanism.
